title: Generative Inverse Design of Metamaterials with Functional Responses by Interpretable Learning
summary: Proposes RIGID, a random-forest-based interpretable generative inverse design method that inverts a forest surrogate to sample metamaterial designs meeting qualitative targets on functional responses such as frequency-dependent behavior, in a single shot and without the large training sets and iterative optimization that deep generative approaches require. The paper's only contact with the SDV lineage is one grouped citation: Xu and Veeramachaneni's TGAN paper appears with two other mixed-type generative models to support the claim that generative and optimization-based inverse design handle mixed continuous and categorical design variables poorly. No SDV code is run and CTGAN is never named, so the entry records a bibliographic reference to TGAN, the predecessor of CTGAN, rather than any use of the SDV stack.
evidence: the results section notes that the problem involves inverse design with both continuous and categorical variables, which common optimization and generative modeling-based inverse design cannot handle well without special treatment, citing the group [86, 87, 88]; reference 88 is Lei Xu and Kalyan Veeramachaneni, Synthesizing tabular data using generative adversarial networks, arXiv:1811.11264, 2018, i.e. TGAN rather than CTGAN; that grouped inline citation is the paper's single SDV-family mention, and the strings CTGAN, SDV and Synthetic Data Vault appear nowhere in the full text

title: Privacy Re-Identification Attacks on Tabular GANs
summary: Investigates how much of a training set can be recovered from the synthetic output of tabular GANs, defining three escalating levels of adversarial knowledge and applying both reconstruction and membership-inference style attacks to synthetic tables generated from Adult, Lending Club, PAKDD and Taiwan credit data, measured by unique samples attacked, hit rate and distance to closest record. CTGAN is one of the three tabular GANs trained and then attacked, alongside CTAB-GAN and CasTGAN, and the paper describes its Wasserstein loss with gradient penalty and its conditional vector selection as the mechanism that models under-represented discrete categories. CTGAN is also the model singled out for the follow-up question on whether attacker-side machine learning predictions improve re-identification, chosen because it is the least expensive of the three to train, so SDV's CTGAN is run as the production generator for a full arm of the study.

title: A Framework for Generating Realistic Synthetic Tabular Data in a Randomized Controlled Trial Setting
summary: Compares two ways of generating synthetic randomized controlled trial data: a simultaneous framework in which a single model produces the whole table, and a sequential framework in which baseline covariates are generated first, treatment is then allocated at random to mimic the trial design, and post-allocation variables including the outcome follow from regression execution models fitted one variable at a time. Three generators are carried through both frameworks, CTGAN, adversarial random forests and an R-vine copula, and the authors conclude that the sequential R-vine copula route best reproduces the features of the real trial data. CTGAN is trained and sampled as one of the compared generation algorithms in both frameworks, and the paper sets out its mode-specific normalization and its conditional generator with training-by-sampling, so an SDV generator is run as a full arm of the study's empirical program.

title: Towards Synthesizing High-Dimensional Tabular Data with Limited Samples
summary: Observes that diffusion-based tabular synthesizers degrade as column count grows, to the point of losing to simpler non-diffusion models, and attributes this to limited training samples in high-dimensional space; proposes CtrTab, which injects data-aware noise into a latent diffusion model as a regularizer and shows analytically that the added noise term acts as a penalty on the gradient of the score network. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the six baselines run against it, alongside SMOTE, TabDDPM, RelDDPM and TabSyn, with competitor hyperparameters taken from the TabSyn paper, and the related-work section credits CTGAN with incorporating class labels in the generator to produce data conditioned on the target class and notes that CTAB-GAN+ extends CTGAN to continuous class labels. CTGAN and TVAE are therefore executed as comparison baselines whose degradation at high dimensionality motivates the proposed model, with nothing of CTGAN carried into CtrTab's architecture.
evidence: figure 1 plots F1 against dimensionality for CtrTab, TabSyn, CTGAN, TVAE, TabDDPM and RelDDPM, showing all existing models decline as dimensions increase; the competitors paragraph lists SMOTE, TVAE (Xu et al. 2019), CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019), TabDDPM, RelDDPM and TabSyn as the six baselines; the related-work section on conditional tabular data synthesis states that CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) incorporates class labels in the generator to produce data conditioned on the target class and that CTAB-GAN+ extends CTGAN to support both discrete and continuous data class labels; the implementation details state that all competitor models are implemented in Python with the same hyperparameter settings as specified in the TabSyn paper

title: Adaptive differentiable trees for transparent learning on data streams
summary: Introduces soft Hoeffding trees, a differentiable and inherently interpretable tree model for online learning that grows in the Hoeffding style while routing instances softly, so it can be trained by gradient descent and adapt to concept drift without losing the readability of a decision path. The evaluation needs long drifting streams that no public dataset supplies, so CTGAN is trained on real tables from the PMLB repository and sampled to emulate their distributions across streams of one million instances, into which ten abrupt drifts are injected by oversampling a randomly chosen class; a further scalability experiment generates ten million drift-free instances the same way. CTGAN is thus run as the data-generation engine for the paper's stream experiments while the paper's own contribution is the tree model, the pattern where an SDV generator powers one part of a study about something else.
evidence: section 5.1.2 states that the streams are derived from real-world data taken from the PMLB repository and that the authors employ a Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN) (Xu et al., 2019) to emulate a realistic distribution within a substantial data stream of 10^6 samples, with abrupt drifts injected by oversampling a randomly selected class and ten drifts induced; the scalability experiment states that data streams containing 10^7 instances were generated using the procedure described in Sect. 5.1.2 with CTGAN, without introducing any drifts; the bibliography carries Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni, Modeling tabular data using conditional GAN, 2019

title: Generating survey databases with Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Networks
summary: Develops Wasserstein GAN variants that carry survey sampling weights through training, so that synthetic records reproduce a weighted survey population rather than the unweighted sample, and evaluates them on the 2019 Belgian Labour Force Survey with 146 variables using Wasserstein distance, FID, SVDD, Cramer-von Mises and KL criteria. CTGAN and CopulaGAN are the two comparison generators the authors did not implement themselves: both are run from the SDV package in Python at default parameters, with the paper pointing readers to the DataCebo GitHub of the Synthetic Data Vault project for the code, and noting that CopulaGAN transforms the data before applying CTGAN and that neither incorporates sampling weights. SDV's generators are therefore executed as the external baselines the weighted models are measured against.

title: A Combinatorial Approach to Synthetic Data Generation for Machine Learning
summary: Presents ComGen, which treats synthetic tabular generation as a combinatorial coverage problem, discretizing each attribute and sampling records that realize every t-way combination of attribute values for t from two to five, plus DP-ComGen, a differentially private variant; the approach is evaluated on travel customer, HELOC, adult income and credit default data for downstream accuracy, statistical similarity and privacy cost. SDV supplies both the baselines and the measuring instruments: TVAE and CopulaGAN are adopted directly from the SDV framework without alterations as the compared generators, and SDV metrics compute the KL divergence and Kolmogorov-Smirnov similarity scores as well as the NumericalMLP and CategoricalKNN privacy-cost metrics. Running SDMetrics as the evaluation harness places this beyond a pure comparison role and makes the whole empirical program dependent on SDV.

title: PPMI-Benchmark: A Dual Evaluation Framework for Imputation and Synthetic Data Generation in Longitudinal Parkinson's Disease Research
summary: Builds a paired benchmark over the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative cohort that evaluates longitudinal imputation methods and synthetic data generators on the same footing, adding sliced Wasserstein distance to the usual fidelity measures and reporting per-center results so that multi-center bias is visible rather than averaged away. Six generation methods are evaluated with the emphasis on CTGAN, whose mode-specific normalization and conditional generation the paper credits for handling mixed clinical data types, and the authors report that CTGAN gave the best preservation of the statistical properties of the PPMI data. Their contribution sits around the generator rather than inside it: the standard CTGAN implementation is run and then enhanced with clinical range constraints on the generated biomarker values, so SDV's CTGAN is the production generator of the framework.
affiliations: Inserm; Université de Lille; Institut Pasteur de Lille; Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Lille
evidence: the keywords list HyperImpute, CTGAN, sliced Wasserstein distance and the PPMI dataset; the contributions list a first comprehensive evaluation of 6 synthetic generation techniques including CTGAN and RTVae adapted for neurodegenerative disease biomarkers; the background states that Conditional Tabular GANs (CTGAN), developed by Xu et al.
